subject: Resilience report and action snapshot: BrightWorks impact Mar 30 outage
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@brightworks.com>, BrightWorks Ops <ops@brightworks.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Resilience report and immediate actions — Mar 30 BrightWorks impact

Hi Amelia / BrightWorks team,

First — thank you for your patience over the last several days. I wanted to share an initial resilience report and the actions we’ve taken so far following the Mar 30th degradation that affected inference latency for some requests. Attached is a short timeline (resilience_timeline_20270405.pdf) and our live action-item tracker.

High-level recap (quick bullets):
- Incident window: Mar 30 09:05–10:40 PDT — customers with sustained long sequences experienced increased 95th percentile latency.
- Impact to BrightWorks: intermittent request timeouts and delayed responses for batch jobs between 09:10–10:05. Your ops team reported retries at ~09:18 which surfaced in your monitoring.
- Immediate mitigations: we routed affected traffic to a compatible model variant, temporarily reduced batch size for your tenant, and applied a hot-fix to autoscaler heuristics to avoid burst-induced queueing.

What you’ll find attached: a concise timeline, who did what and when, and an action tracker with owners and ETA. We’ll follow up with a more detailed RCA and a technical appendix from engineering.

Next steps from Redwood (short):
1) Today — deliver the full RCA and technical appendix (Connor leading).
2) By Apr 9 — permanent autoscaler config change + accompanying load test report.
3) By Apr 30 — longer-term change: KV-cache enhancement and fallback routing improvements.

I’m copying Stephanie who is coordinating account comms and Markus from reliability who can weigh in on SLAs and credits. If you prefer a call to walk through the timeline, I’m available tomorrow morning.

Apologies again for the disruption. We are treating this as high priority and will keep you updated hourly while we finalize artifacts.

—
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales (EMEA & Strategic Accounts)
Redwood Inference
(attachment: resilience_timeline_20270405.pdf)
From: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@brightworks.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightWorks Ops <ops@brightworks.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Resilience report and immediate actions — Mar 30 BrightWorks impact

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the quick summary. A couple of clarifying questions before we dig into the timeline:

- When you say "compatible model variant" — did you move our requests to a quantized model or a different architecture? We noticed a slight change in output tokenization for one of our pipelines.
- Can you confirm whether any customer data was retried or reprocessed beyond the normal autoscaler retry window? Our compliance team is asking specifically.

If it helps, ops can share a brief log extract from 09:15–09:30 showing the connection resets we saw. We’d like to align on whether the change in batch size could have altered exactly-once semantics for in-flight requests.

—Amelia
Amelia Ross
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightWorks
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@brightworks.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 17:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Resilience report and immediate actions — Mar 30 BrightWorks impact

Amelia — thanks for the questions. See quick answers below; Connor will send the engineering appendix with precise technical details.

- "Compatible model variant": we routed traffic to a lower-precision quantized variant of the same model family (fp16->int8-style profile). That change can shift tokenization in rare edge prompts. We scrubbed a sample of outputs for BrightWorks and did not see material semantic changes, but we will include diff samples in the appendix.

- Retries and data reprocessing: there was no replay of customer inputs beyond the standard retry window. Autoscaler retries were invoked (up to 3 attempts) for some in-flight requests; we have audit logs tied to your tenant showing retry attempts and their statuses. We will share the log extract you mentioned — please send the extract and Connor will correlate.

Connor — can you take point on the appendix and include: exact kernel/quantization profile used, request ids for the affected window, and the audit-log snippets we can share with BrightWorks?

On the process side, Stephanie will lead a short remediation sync with BrightWorks ops tomorrow to confirm remaining compensations/credits if any. Markus — can you confirm the SLA impact calculation and whether a recovery credit is appropriate under our contract?

On call availability: we can do 09:00–10:00 PDT tomorrow.

—
Marissa

Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Engineering appendix — Mar 30 performance regression (technical notes)

Hi Amelia / BrightWorks team — Connor here from Platform Reliability. Thanks for the quick coordination yesterday. Below is the condensed technical appendix followed by the immediate and planned engineering actions; I’ve attached the action tracker for owner/ETA.

Root cause (brief):
- On Mar 30 at 09:04:22 PDT a recent autoscaler heuristic intended to reduce tail latency interacted poorly with our burst queue estimation when warmup sequences exceeded 2x the median length. This caused queue head-of-line blocking on a subset of GPU workers and delayed KV cache population for affected sessions.

Observed impact to BrightWorks:
- Your tenant saw delayed completions and timeouts for sequences >512 tokens. Approximately 4.6% of requests in the window experienced latency >10s; ~0.9% timed out before retry.

Mitigations performed (Mar 30 morning):
- 09:10 PDT: applied temporary autoscaler parameter rollback to prior safe profile.
- 09:22 PDT: shifted BrightWorks traffic to the int8-compatible variant to reduce per-token compute pressure.
- 09:35 PDT: lowered batch size for your tenant to prevent head-of-line blocking.

What we will deliver in the full RCA:
- Exact autoscaler commit id and diff, kernel selection logs, and request ids for correlation.
- Diffed outputs for a representative sample (your flagged prompts).
- Audit log extract showing retry attempts and statuses for your tenant.

Immediate follow-ups (owners / ETA):
- Connor: full kernel & commit-level appendix (24 hours) — will include artifacts to reproduce locally.
- Markus: SLA impact calc and proposed credit (48 hours).
- Stephanie: customer remediation proposal and optional call scheduling (today).

Planned engineering changes (timeline):
- Apr 9: permanent autoscaler rule update plus unit load tests against long-sequence workloads.
- Apr 23: KV-cache warming optimization to reduce cold-population delays.
- May 14: rollout of improved fallback routing that avoids model-variant switching for stateful sessions.

Attachments: action_item_tracker_brightworks.xlsx (live tracker).

If you want a deep-dive call, I can walk through the kernel logs and the reproducer tests.

—
Connor O'Brien
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: action_item_tracker_brightworks.xlsx)

Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Engineering appendix — Mar 30 performance regression (technical notes)

Connor — this is helpful, thanks. A few follow-ups from our side:

1) Can you include the exact request ids and the sample diffs you mentioned so we can validate end-to-end?
2) Our compliance team still wants confirmation there was no replay of PII-marked payloads beyond retries. Can you include a brief statement in the appendix about data handling during retries (redwood internal policy reference if helpful)?

We’re open to the Apr 9 config change timeline and would like to be part of the load-test window. Please add our ops account to the test plan.

We remain concerned about model-variant switching during customer sessions; if that remains a recommended mitigation in some scenarios, we need a clear policy statement and a guarantee that outputs will be diffed and stored for 30 days for customer inspection.

—Amelia
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@brightworks.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Final commitments and next steps — BrightWorks resilience report

Amelia — thanks again for the constructive collaboration. Quick commitments and next steps from Redwood:  

1) Appendix delivery: Connor will post the full RCA (including request ids, kernel diffs, and audit-log snippets) by 2027-04-06 09:00 PDT — link will be shared to the Drive reference above.
2) Data handling statement: we confirm that retries were limited to standard autoscaler retry semantics and did not trigger wide replays; Connor will add a short data-handling paragraph referencing our internal data processing policy.
3) Load-test participation: BrightWorks ops will be added to the Apr 9 test plan; Stephanie will send the invite and runbook by Apr 7.
4) Output diff retention: we will retain diff artifacts for 30 days and give your ops a read-only link; Markus will confirm in a follow-up the storage path and access controls.
5) SLA credit: Markus will propose a credit calculation by Apr 7; we will aim to finalize any agreed credit within 7 business days thereafter.

We will treat these deliverables as high priority. If anything in the tracker needs adjusting, Stephanie will own reconciling with BrightWorks. I’m available for a wrap call next Friday if you’d like.

Best —
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales (EMEA & Strategic Accounts)
Redwood Inference
